security_audit.summary: Most Markdown backtick, localhost URL, and fixed artifact path alerts are false positives in examples. The real risks are command execution in scripts/with_server.py and prompt-injection-like guidance discouraging source review before execution. No evidence of external data exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: Server commands are passed to subprocess.Popen with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid shell=True where possible, accept command arrays, or restrict server commands to trusted allowlisted scripts.

remediation.issue: The helper runs arbitrary post-start commands from command-line arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation and document that generated or untrusted commands must be inspected before execution.

remediation.issue: Skill guidance tells agents not to read helper source before trying scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Remove black-box-only guidance and instruct agents to inspect helper behavior before executing command-capable scripts.

remediation.issue: Examples save screenshots and console logs to local artifact paths.
remediation.suggestion: Document that artifacts may contain sensitive UI data, console output, or tokens and should be reviewed before sharing.

content.user_title: Test Local Web Apps with Playwright
content.value_statement: Manual browser checks miss dynamic UI issues and console errors. This skill guides Playwright scripts for local app inspection, screenshots, logs, and selector-based actions.
actual_capabilities: Guides native Python Playwright scripts for local browser testing.
Starts one or more local servers before running an automation command.
Captures browser console messages during automated page interaction.
Discovers visible buttons, links, and form fields on rendered pages.
Captures screenshots for dynamic pages and static HTML files.
Demonstrates file:// testing for local static HTML documents.
limitations: It focuses on local applications and static HTML, not hosted production monitoring.
It requires Playwright and browser dependencies to be installed separately.
The server helper can execute local commands and should use trusted inputs only.
It does not provide built-in accessibility, performance, or security scoring.

use_cases.title: Debug a Local Frontend
use_cases.description: Inspect rendered UI state, capture screenshots, and review console output while a development server is running.

use_cases.title: Verify Basic User Flows
use_cases.description: Run Playwright actions against buttons, links, forms, and navigation after the app reaches network idle.

use_cases.title: Automate Static HTML Checks
use_cases.description: Open local HTML files through file URLs, interact with elements, and save before-and-after screenshots.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Running Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check of an existing local server.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the webapp-testing skill to inspect my running local app at http://localhost:5173. Capture a screenshot and list visible buttons, links, and inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Console Logs
prompt_templates.scenario: Debug browser console output during a simple interaction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the webapp-testing skill to open my local app, click the Dashboard link, wait for the page to settle, and summarize any console messages.

prompt_templates.title: Run With a Dev Server
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate test when the server is not already running.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the webapp-testing skill to start my frontend with npm run dev on port 5173, then run a Playwright check that verifies the main form renders.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Multi-Service Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with separate backend and frontend services.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the webapp-testing skill to start my backend on port 3000 and frontend on port 5173, then verify login, dashboard loading, and console errors.

output_examples.input: Inspect http://localhost:5173 and find interactive elements.
output: Screenshot captured for the rendered page.
Found primary navigation links, two visible buttons, and three form fields.
Suggested stable selectors for the next automation step.

output_examples.input: Capture console logs while clicking Dashboard.
output: The page loaded after network idle.
Console output was saved and summarized, including warnings and errors.

output_examples.input: Open a local static HTML file and submit the sample form.
output: The file was opened through a local file URL.
Before and after screenshots were captured.
The form fields were filled and submitted successfully.

best_practices: Wait for network idle or a stable selector before inspecting dynamic pages.
Use descriptive role, text, CSS, or ID selectors that match rendered UI.
Review helper commands before running them, especially when prompts provide server strings.
anti_patterns: Do not run server commands from untrusted prompts without inspection.
Do not inspect dynamic pages before JavaScript has finished rendering key content.
Do not store screenshots or console logs that may contain secrets without review.

faq.question: What does this skill test?
faq.answer: It helps test local web pages with Playwright by opening pages, inspecting elements, taking screenshots, and capturing console logs.

faq.question: Does it start my local server?
faq.answer: Yes. The bundled helper can start one or more server commands, wait for ports, run a test command, and stop the servers.

faq.question: Can it test static HTML files?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show opening local HTML files through file URLs and interacting with page elements.

faq.question: Does it require Playwright?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use Python Playwright, so Playwright and browser dependencies must be available.

faq.question: Is it safe to run on any project?
faq.answer: Use trusted projects and inspect server commands first. The helper can execute local commands that you provide.

faq.question: Does it replace a full test suite?
faq.answer: No. It is best for targeted browser checks, debugging, and exploration before writing durable tests.
